notes: THE DEFECT WAS ONE LINE WITH TWO CLIFFS IN IT. pnrPair picked its handler out of `five.filter((p) => p.attrs.playvol >= 70 && p.attrs.height <= 78)`, and handlerFit itself carries no height term at all, so height was priced NOWHERE except in that filter — as a veto. Measured by one-point perturbation of the pnr/pickpop fit over five pinned fives, main's two biggest discontinuities in the whole two-man game are exactly those two gates: 42.02 points of fit for one inch of height (Magic '87, 78 -> 79) and 25.00 for one point of play volume (Westbrook '16, 69 -> 70). The men the height half forbade from running a pick-and-roll at all: Magic '87 (playvol 98), Jokic '25 (97), LeBron '18 (95), Simmons '18 (90), Giannis '21 (79) and the subject, Durant '16 (70 — he cleared the other half EXACTLY, so height alone excluded him). The playvol half was worse than a cliff: it was the only way this function could return `handler: null`, and a null makes the fit's 0.40-weighted handler term read ZERO. That happened on 321 of the wheel's 1,255 fives — an IMPOSSIBLE pick-and-roll where the truth is a BAD one.

THE FIX MAKES THE OLD GATES THE ENDS OF TWO RAMPS, so no man who was eligible before loses a decimal: `height <= 78` becomes the FOOT of PNR_H0..PNR_H1 (78 -> 82, recal_213's own band, the ramp hornsHandler already reads the other way round) and `playvol >= 70` becomes the TOP of PNR_PV0..PNR_PV1 (60 -> 70) with a 0.15 FLOOR so the score never reaches zero and a five of five non-passers still nominates the best of them. pnrHandler = handlerFit x ballShare x (1 - 0.65 x heightRamp): Durant '16 22.4, Magic '87 50.7, Jokic '25 34.6, Murray '25 61.8. There is no filter left — the handler is the argmax of one continuous monotone score over all five men and can never be null (0 of 1,255 after, 321 before).

THE NOMINATION IS DISCOUNTED AND A NAMED MAN IS NOT. handlerRead scales the handler term of the fit only when NOBODY named a pair, because one question answers both halves of an auto-pick: who runs it, and how much of a pick-and-roll it is. A CALLED pair prices on handlerFit, height-free and ball-share-free — recal_124's doctrine verbatim, and what makes "KD can run pnr" worth calling: naming Durant + Freedom on the four-man cast reads 61.72 fit / +0.39 points where the engine's own read of the same five is 45.72 / -1.37. recal_208's iso already carries exactly this asymmetry (the engine will not nominate Embiid, a plan that names him is priced at his full isoScore and beats the engine's read); the difference here is that this one is a ramp, so a five with a 6'9" handler falls DOWN the style smoothly instead of out of it. It is ALSO what holds the Lakers '87 helio pin: Magic is nominated (which the ruling asks for) while the Showtime pick-and-roll reads 62.0 against their pinned helio 67.0.

THE THREE RULINGS, EACH ACCOUNTABLE ON ITS OWN, on the wheel's 1,255 fieldable fives. The two GATES alone (HAND_TILT set to 0): 329 pairs move, 8 READS move, pnr 269 -> 274, pickpop 37 -> 40. The TILT on top moves 21 more reads and brings pnr back down to 258. Every moved pair attributed by lifting ONE gate at a time: the HEIGHT half alone would move 4 (Blazers '92 Porter -> Drexler, Mavericks '23 Dinwiddie -> Doncic, Bulls '26 Jones -> Giddey, Lakers '84 NONE -> Magic), the PLAYVOL half alone 249 (every one of them a five where nobody cleared playvol 70, so there was no handler at all), and 76 are reached by both — those had no handler AND a tall passer, and the man who ends up with the ball comes from the HEIGHT half on 66 of them (Magic's Lakers '83-'91, Bird's Celtics '84-'86, Pippen's Bulls '94-'98, Hardaway's Magic, Grant Hill's Pistons, McGrady's Magic and Rockets, LeBron's Cavaliers and Lakers, Jokic's Nuggets, Luka's Mavericks, Simmons's Sixers, Giannis's Bucks, LaMelo's Hornets) and from the PLAYVOL half on 10. 321 fives had a null handler before; 0 do now.

THE WHEEL DISTRIBUTION, shipped main -> after: balanced 357 -> 361, pnr 269 -> 258, postup 204 -> 207, helio 120 -> 120, iso 51 -> 51, dho 48 -> 48, pindown 46 -> 46, motion 44 -> 44, pickpop 37 -> 39, horns 33 -> 36, triangle 30 -> 29, fiveout 16 -> 16. 29 of 1,255 reads change (2.3%), and the pick-and-roll's reach FALLS rather than rises: the gates add 5 reads and the tilt takes 16 back off, because the tilt is a penalty on the wrong call and never a bonus on the right one, so no five's pnr fit can rise from it. Only 4 fives change read between the roll and the pop, which is the tilt's own count: Suns '01, Thunder '15 and Grizzlies '23 to the pop, Mavericks '04 to the roll.

THE PIN THAT MOVES, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE: THUNDER '15, pnr -> pickpop. recal_214's receipt recorded that five as an EXACT TIE — Ibaka '15's efficiency 58 caps both screener terms, so pnr and pickpop both read 71.40 and the read stayed pnr only because pick-and-roll is listed first in STYLES. This round's third ruling breaks that tie by naming the man who breaks it: Westbrook '15 is 3pt 38 / rim 76, the downhill man, so his ROLL is docked 3 (99.0 -> 96.0) and his pop is not, giving pnr 70.20 against pickpop 71.40. His older ruling on that five ("Pnr for 15' Thunder when Steven adams in the corner cant be the main tactic as his def will sag off him") is about WHERE ADAMS STANDS, and that is untouched: the pair is Westbrook + Ibaka in both calls, the drawing is identical (tests/court.test.ts pins spotsFor pickpop === spotsFor pnr) and Adams stands in the paint either way. Exactly the supersession recal_214 made when his Durant/Westbrook ruling re-pointed THUNDER_16 from pnr to pickpop. HIS WORD DECIDES: setting HAND_TILT to 0 restores the tie and the pnr read, and costs the third ruling entirely.

EVERY OTHER PINNED READ HOLDS, measured through bestStyle on the wheel's own starting fives: Jazz '97 pnr (76.25, recal_120's number to the decimal, because Stockton '97 is 3pt 73 / rim 53 — a ROLL handler — and his term is not docked at all), Nuggets '25 pnr (72.94, unmoved, Murray handling and Jokic screening), Thunder '25 pnr, Suns '05 pnr, Rockets '18 pnr, Thunder '16 pickpop (80.48 against the roll's 75.14, a wider preference than recal_214 left), Magic '11 postup (81.63 against pnr 81.50 — a 0.13-point read, and the reason the tilt is a penalty and not a signed credit), Hornets '95 postup, Pelicans '16 postup, Celtics '25 fiveout, Thunder '22 helio, Lakers '87 helio, Bulls '96 and '97 triangle, Raptors '17 iso, Nets '23 iso, Jazz '81 iso, Knicks '84 iso, Spurs '16 balanced, Pistons '07 motion, Wolves '97 / Kings '02 / Grizzlies '17 horns, Pacers '96 / Warriors '16 / Knicks '02 pindown, Kings '24 / Bulls '14 / Sixers '18 dho.

TWO KNOBS ARE BOUNDED BY PINS AND THE BOUNDS ARE REPORTED, NOT TUNED AROUND (the practice recal_213 used for HORN_BASE). PNR_HDISC 0.65: under 0.48 the Showtime Lakers' own auto pick-and-roll clears the helio their ruling pinned (67.76 against 67.00 at 0.45), and under 0.38 Jokic outscores Murray and takes Denver's ball; what stops it climbing is that at 1.00 a 6'10" man's nomination is ZERO and the ramp is the old veto in disguise. PNR_PV0 60: it is the GENTLEST foot that leaves the Nets '23 in the iso recal_208's ruling put them in — Irving '23 is playvol 68, two points under the old floor, and at a foot of 58 his pick-and-roll reads 68.4 against their iso 68.1 and the pin breaks. At 60 it is 66.7 against 68.1, a 1.4-point margin, and that margin is the thinnest thing in this round.

THE TILT'S SHAPE WAS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN. Two forms were tried first and both break a pin. SIGNED about the midpoint (handlerFit +- HAND_TILT/2): Magic '11's post-up is a 0.13-point read and Jameer Nelson '11 is a pure shooter, so ANY credit on the roll side takes that five off the post (81.91 against 81.63) and it also widens the Nuggets '25 pnr-over-horns margin to 3.10, past the 2.5 recal_213 pinned as HORN_BASE's own cap. ONE-SIDED off the RAW credit (-HAND_TILT x (1 - credit)): every handler who is not both a shooter and a driver pays in BOTH calls, so the pick-and-roll loses 19 wheel reads instead of 11. The landed form docks each call by how much better SUITED the man is to the OTHER one, so the call he is built for prices him at exactly the handlerFit he had before this round: max(rollHandler, popHandler) === handlerFit for every card, and no pnr fit anywhere can rise. Measured, base -> roll / pop: Westbrook '16 99.0 -> 96.2 / 99.0 (the POP, his ruling), Durant '16 64.1 -> 64.1 / 62.0 (the ROLL, the other half of the same line), Stockton '97 87.1 -> 87.1 / 84.1 (the ROLL), Giannis '21 70.4 -> 67.4 / 70.4, Jokic '25 99.0 -> 99.0 / 99.0 (both, and the 99 clamp says so), LeBron '18 99.0 -> 98.1 / 99.0, Draymond '16 49.8 -> 49.8 / 47.5.

NO CLIFF REPLACES THE CLIFF, and the proof is the same perturbation table that found it. Worst one-point jump in the pnr/pickpop fit over five pinned fives, per attribute, main -> after: height 42.02 -> 19.32, playvol 25.00 -> 21.36, volume 3.67 -> 4.87, efficiency 4.40 -> 4.40, rim 4.05 -> 4.05, 3pt 2.59 -> 2.59, mid 0.35 -> 0.35. Both remaining leaders are SLOT crossings and neither is a price: the 19.32 is a man crossing the SCREENER's own height line of 80 (Hornacek '97 at 79 -> 80), which is not in his ruling and is left alone, and the 21.36 is the allocation defect recal_214 left for its own round — the nomination changing hands re-assigns the screen. Pinned in tests/tactics.test.ts at < 22 over 5 fives x 5 men x 7 attributes x 100 values x 2 calls.

ONE MAN CANNOT BE BOTH, which is new only because the round makes it possible: the old pools were disjoint by construction (handler <= 78, screener >= 80). On 26 wheel fives the nominated handler is also the best screener on the floor (Jokic, LeBron, Luka, Magic, Pippen). He keeps the BALL, which is the slot his nomination won, and the screen goes to the next big — UNLESS he is the five's only big, in which case the screen is a slot nobody else can fill and the ball goes to the second nominee instead (Nuggets '19 and '20, where Jokic is the whole front court: he screens, Murray handles). Without that second clause those two fives lost their screener entirely and 30 points of fit with it. After both clauses: 0 fives with a null handler, 0 with a null screener that had a big, and handler !== screener everywhere.

THE DRAWING IS FIXED WHERE THE GATE BROKE IT, and NOT where it was blamed. On main the 321 no-handler fives drew a pick-and-roll with nobody on the ball: the Lakers '87 stood BYRON SCOTT on the ball spot while pnrPair returned handler undefined, so the number and the floor named different men. After: Magic '87 holds the ball in the fit, the drawing and the caption. But the Lakers '80 and '81 are NOT this bug, and the measurement overrules the hypothesis: Magic '80 is playvol 75 / handlerFit 57.2 against NORM NIXON '80 at 58.0 (and '81: 60.0 against 65.1), so Nixon is the better handler on the base term before any height discount, at every value of PNR_HDISC from 0 to 1. Those two fives read horns anyway, and in a called pick-and-roll Magic still takes the dunker spot — because the second-year Magic card is a 75-playvol off-guard beside a point guard, not because of the gate this round removed. That drawing belongs to recal_212's rank (height + orb) or to the '80/'81 cards, and it is reported here rather than fixed in the wrong file.

NOTHING REGENERATES AND NO RATING MOVES.
